sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: A bombshell legal settlement reached a few days ago is about to change almost everything about buying and selling a home.
sentences.zh: 几天前达成的一项重磅法律和解协议，即将改变房屋买卖的几乎所有方面。

sentences.en: and, in the process, make it significantly cheaper.
sentences.zh: 并在此过程中，使其成本大幅降低。

sentences.en: My colleague, Debra Kamen, explains.
sentences.zh: 我的同事黛布拉·卡门为您解读。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, March 20th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月20日，星期三。

sentences.en: Hi, Debra.
sentences.zh: 你好，黛布拉。

sentences.en: Hi, Michael.
sentences.zh: 你好，迈克尔。

sentences.en: What a treat.
sentences.zh: 真是难得。

sentences.en: Talk of this, it's surreal.
sentences.zh: 谈论这个，感觉太不真实了。

sentences.en: Do you want me just to go?
sentences.zh: 你想让我直接开始吗？

sentences.en: No, I'm going to ask you a question.
sentences.zh: 不，我要先问你一个问题。

sentences.en: I'm ready.
sentences.zh: 我准备好了。

sentences.en: This is a conversation.
sentences.zh: 这是一场对话。

sentences.en: I came ready to roll.
sentences.zh: 我已蓄势待发。

sentences.en: What do you want from me?
sentences.zh: 你想从我这得到什么？

sentences.en: So, Debra, at the highest possible level, what just happened to American real estate?
sentences.zh: 那么，黛布拉，从最高层面来看，美国房地产市场刚刚发生了什么？

sentences.en: Michael, there's been this invisible hand that's been guiding and controlling the real estate industry for over 100 years.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，有一只无形的手在过去100多年里一直引导和控制着房地产行业。

sentences.en: And they have long thought that they were absolutely untouchable because they had so much power, so much influence, so much money.
sentences.zh: 他们长期以来认为自己绝对不可撼动，因为他们拥有巨大的权力、巨大的影响力，以及巨额的资金。

sentences.en: And the biggest crack in their armor that's ever happened just happened on Friday.
sentences.zh: 而他们防线中出现的最大裂痕，就在周五刚刚发生了。

sentences.en: Well, what is this crack in the armor?
sentences.zh: 那么，这个裂痕到底是什么？

sentences.en: And I guess who even is this nefarious sounding group that you're talking about?
sentences.zh: 还有，你提到的这个听起来很邪恶的组织到底是谁？

sentences.en: The group is the National Association of Realtors.
sentences.zh: 这个组织就是全美房地产经纪人协会（NAR）。

sentences.en: Nearly 9 out of 10 home sales are handled by real estate agents affiliated with NAR.
sentences.zh: 近90%的房屋销售是由隶属于NAR的房地产经纪人处理的。

sentences.en: And the crack in the armor is that they have had these rules that have controlled how much buyers and sellers pay to their agents and how you work with agents to get a home on the market.
sentences.zh: 所谓的裂痕在于，他们一直有这些规则，控制着买家和卖家支付给经纪人的费用，以及你如何与经纪人合作将房屋投放市场。

sentences.en: And then last week, for the first time in its history, NAR's control over this huge industry basically collapsed.
sentences.zh: 而上周，NAR对这个庞大行业的控制力历史上首次基本崩溃了。

sentences.en: And with it, so did many of the costs it was imposing on consumers.
sentences.zh: 随之崩溃的，还有他们强加给消费者的许多成本。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This sounds huge.
sentences.zh: 这听起来影响巨大。

sentences.en: I think we need to slow this whole thing down.
sentences.zh: 我想我们需要放慢节奏，把整件事理清楚。

sentences.en: And I think the way to do that is to have you tell us the story of how the National Association of Realtors, which is not at all a household name,
sentences.zh: 我觉得最好的方式是请你讲讲全美房地产经纪人协会的故事——尽管它一点也不是家喻户晓的名字——

sentences.en: became such a powerful force in the ritual of buying and selling a home in the United States.
sentences.zh: 它是如何在美国房屋买卖的惯例中成为如此强大的力量的。

sentences.en: The NAR is huge.
sentences.zh: NAR非常庞大。

sentences.en: Over their existence, they've grown to 1.5 million members.
sentences.zh: 在他们存在期间，会员人数已增长到150万。

sentences.en: More importantly, they've created a system where you really cannot sell a house unless you're a member.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，他们建立了一个系统，除非你是会员，否则你真的无法卖掉房子。

sentences.en: They even own the word Realtor.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至拥有“Realtor”（房地产经纪人）这个词的商标权。

sentences.en: They own the word Realtor?
sentences.zh: 他们拥有“Realtor”这个词？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They even had a campaign a couple years ago to convince people how to say it properly and correctly.
sentences.zh: 几年前他们甚至发起了一场运动，教人们如何正确地发音。

sentences.en: They take this very seriously.
sentences.zh: 他们对此非常认真。

sentences.en: Okay, okay, I'll bite.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧，我上钩了。

sentences.en: How do you say it properly?
sentences.zh: 怎么发音才正确？

sentences.en: It's Realtor, not Realtor.
sentences.zh: 是Realtor，不是Re-al-tor。

sentences.en: Realtor?
sentences.zh: Realtor？

sentences.en: Two syllables, not three.
sentences.zh: 两个音节，不是三个。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Very important.
sentences.zh: 非常重要。

sentences.en: Extremely important.
sentences.zh: 极其重要。

sentences.en: So I should say, on paper, you can sell a house if you're not a Realtor.
sentences.zh: 所以我应该说，从书面上看，如果你不是Realtor，你也可以卖房子。

sentences.en: if you're just a real estate agent.
sentences.zh: 如果你只是个房地产经纪人。

sentences.en: And not a member of NAR.
sentences.zh: 而且不是NAR的会员。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But in practice, it's really not that easy because of the system they've created.
sentences.zh: 但在实践中，由于他们建立的系统，这真的没那么容易。

sentences.en: They make it very difficult.
sentences.zh: 他们让事情变得非常困难。

sentences.en: For example, if you want to list a home for sale, you have to put it on something called an MLS, a multiple listing service.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你想挂牌出售房屋，你必须把它放在所谓的MLS（多重上市服务系统）上。

sentences.en: And MLSs, for the most part, are owned and operated by the local subsidiaries of NAR.
sentences.zh: 而MLS在很大程度上是由NAR的当地分支机构拥有和运营的。

sentences.en: They control the databases in which homes basically enter the market.
sentences.zh: 他们控制着房屋进入市场的数据库。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And not only the databases in which homes enter the market,
sentences.zh: 不仅是房屋进入市场的数据库，

sentences.en: but the databases through which realtors tell each other how much commission they will get paid if they sell those homes.
sentences.zh: 还是房地产经纪人互相告知如果卖掉这些房子能获得多少佣金的数据库。

sentences.en: And the databases are very important because databases are where real estate agents can see how much commission they will make if they bring a buyer or they sell a home.
sentences.zh: 这些数据库非常重要，因为房地产经纪人可以在数据库中看到，如果他们带来买家或卖掉房子，他们能赚多少佣金。

sentences.en: Typically, when you sell a house in the U.S., you pay a commission fee.
sentences.zh: 通常在美国卖房时，你需要支付佣金。

sentences.en: It's usually around 5% or 6% to realtors.
sentences.zh: 通常是给经纪人的5%或6%。

sentences.en: This is how realtors are making their money.
sentences.zh: 这就是经纪人赚钱的方式。

sentences.en: It's what you're paying them for everything they're doing, listing the house, showing the house, and it's how they make a living.
sentences.zh: 这是你为他们所做的一切支付的报酬，包括挂牌、带看，这也是他们谋生的手段。

sentences.en: But it's a very high rate.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个非常高的比例。

sentences.en: 5% or 6% is one of the highest rates in the world.
sentences.zh: 5%或6%是世界上最高的费率之一。

sentences.en: Almost no other developed country has a rate that high.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有其他发达国家的费率有这么高。

sentences.en: Okay, and let's talk about 6% for just a minute.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们来谈谈6%这个数字。

sentences.en: That's a number everyone knows if you've ever especially sold a home because it's a number you hate.
sentences.zh: 如果你卖过房子，每个人都知道这个数字，因为这是一个你讨厌的数字。

sentences.en: You hate the fact, no offense to realtors, that you have to give 6% of the money you get for your home to a real estate agent.
sentences.zh: 你讨厌这样一个事实——无意冒犯经纪人——你必须把你卖房所得的6%交给房地产经纪人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, two relative agents.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是给两位相关经纪人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Because it gets split.
sentences.zh: 因为它是平分的。

sentences.en: Half goes to the seller agent, half goes to the buyer agent.
sentences.zh: 一半给卖方经纪人，一半给买方经纪人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And just to put it in perspective, because I think it's useful, if you're selling a million-dollar house, 6% fee is $60,000.
sentences.zh: 为了有个概念，我觉得这很有用，如果你卖一套100万美元的房子，6%的费用就是6万美元。

sentences.en: If you're selling a half-million-dollar house, it's $30,000.
sentences.zh: 如果你卖一套50万美元的房子，就是3万美元。

sentences.en: Either way you slice it, it's a lot of money to put in somebody else's pocket for a huge investment that you made.
sentences.zh: 无论怎么算，对于你所做的巨大投资来说，这都是一大笔钱，进了别人的口袋。

sentences.en: You're trying to get the money into your pocket, but it's coming out of your pocket and going to the agent.
sentences.zh: 你本想把钱放进自己的口袋，但它却从你的口袋里流向了经纪人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You're saying the National Association of Realtors should be seen as essentially the force behind that 6% fee, the loathed 6% fee, staying what it has been for so long.
sentences.zh: 你是说全美房地产经纪人协会本质上应该被视为那6%佣金背后的推手，正是因为他们，这个令人厌恶的6%费率才长期维持不变。

sentences.en: NAR will say, we never set 6%.
sentences.zh: NAR会说，我们从未设定过6%。

sentences.en: We don't have 6% set in stone.
sentences.zh: 我们没有把6%定死。

sentences.en: That is true.
sentences.zh: 这确实是真的。

sentences.en: But they created rules that led to a system where that 6% has become the industry standard, and anyone trying to challenge it, their business model has fallen apart.
sentences.zh: 但他们制定的规则导致了一个系统，使得6%成为了行业标准，任何试图挑战它的人，其商业模式都会土崩瓦解。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: And here's how they control the market.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们控制市场的方式。

sentences.en: For example, if you're a real estate agent and you want to open that home for a customer, in most markets, NAR controls the lockboxes that you use to open the homes.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你是一名房地产经纪人，想为客户打开那间房子，在大多数市场，NAR控制着你用来开门的密码锁盒。

sentences.en: Everyone knows what those lockboxes look like with the little punch key.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道那种带小按键的密码锁盒长什么样。

sentences.en: NAR actually owns one of the two companies in America that makes those lockboxes.
sentences.zh: NAR实际上拥有美国两家生产这种锁盒的公司之一。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And in many markets, they require their agents to use their own technology.
sentences.zh: 在许多市场，他们要求经纪人使用他们自己的技术。

sentences.en: So every aspect of the home selling transaction, from the very beginning to the very end, that hand of NAR is guiding it and behind it.
sentences.zh: 所以房屋销售交易的每一个环节，从头到尾，都有NAR那只手在引导和背后操控。

sentences.en: And it's been there for 100 years.
sentences.zh: 而且这种情况已经持续了100年。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, that sounds an awful lot like monopolistic level of power.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来非常像垄断级别的权力。

sentences.en: The word monopoly gets thrown around all the time when critics are talking about NAR.
sentences.zh: 当批评者谈论NAR时，“垄断”这个词经常被提起。

sentences.en: Another word that comes up a lot is the word cartel.
sentences.zh: 另一个经常出现的词是“卡特尔”。

sentences.en: There's a lot of power, there's a lot of control, and there's also a very organized drive to go after anyone who tries to challenge them.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有巨大的权力、巨大的控制力，而且还有一种非常有组织的动力去打击任何试图挑战他们的人。

sentences.en: This is just not a level of influence that I associate with the trade group.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是我印象中行业协会应有的影响力水平。

sentences.en: I think of trade groups as kind of gathering people together for professional development.
sentences.zh: 我以为行业协会只是把人们聚在一起进行专业交流。

sentences.en: And having a happy hour at the hotel.
sentences.zh: 然后在酒店喝喝欢乐时光的酒。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Not controlling A to Z elements of the industry.
sentences.zh: 而不是控制行业从A到Z的所有要素。

sentences.en: If there was an NAR in journalism, it sounds like they would control the printing presses.
sentences.zh: 如果新闻界也有一个NAR，听起来他们会控制印刷机。

sentences.en: How is it possible that no private company has come along and tried to break into this NAR-controlled market?
sentences.zh: 怎么可能没有私营公司尝试打破这个由NAR控制的市场？

sentences.en: Or that the government hasn't looked at it and thought, cartel, monopoly, we've got to bust this up?
sentences.zh: 或者政府没有审视它并认为：这是卡特尔、是垄断，我们必须拆散它？

sentences.en: People have definitely tried.
sentences.zh: 人们绝对尝试过。

sentences.en: So it's not that it's people have not tried.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是人们没有尝试过。

sentences.en: The challenge is that NAR, because they have so much power, they have quashed any attempts at challenging them.
sentences.zh: 挑战在于，NAR因为权力太大，他们扼杀了任何挑战他们的企图。

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: They sue the heck out of anybody who comes after them.
sentences.zh: 他们会起诉任何敢于挑战他们的人。

sentences.en: There have been upstart companies that have tried to advertise homes outside of these multiple listing services that NAR controls.
sentences.zh: 曾有一些初创公司试图在NAR控制的这些多重上市服务系统之外发布房源广告。

sentences.en: And NAR has sued them.
sentences.zh: 而NAR起诉了他们。

sentences.en: And then you get buried in tens of thousands of dollars of legal fees for an upstart tech company.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会被数万美元的法律费用压垮，对于一家初创科技公司来说，这太沉重了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's a death blow.
sentences.zh: 那是致命一击。

sentences.en: What about the government?
sentences.zh: 那政府呢？

sentences.en: The government has also been going after NAR for more than 20 years.
sentences.zh: 政府也已经追查NAR超过20年了。

sentences.en: The DOJ and NAR have been locked into battle back and forth since 2005.
sentences.zh: 司法部和NAR自2005年以来就一直陷入拉锯战。

sentences.en: But in terms of the government, NAR is not just a trade organization.
sentences.zh: 但就政府而言，NAR不仅仅是一个行业组织。

sentences.en: They are also a political action committee.
sentences.zh: 他们也是一个政治行动委员会。

sentences.en: They have the largest pack in Washington in terms of dollars raised, and they give millions of dollars to candidates who are in line with their agenda,
sentences.zh: 就筹集的资金而言，他们在华盛顿拥有最大的政治行动委员会，他们向符合其议程的候选人捐赠数百万美元，

sentences.en: and they spend millions of dollars fighting candidates who are not in line with their agenda.
sentences.zh: 并花费数百万美元打击那些不符合其议程的候选人。

sentences.en: So anyone in the government who wants to go after NAR knows that they are fighting a battle that probably is bigger and more moneyed than they really want to deal with.
sentences.zh: 所以任何想对付NAR的政府官员都知道，他们正在打一场可能比他们真正想处理的规模更大、资金更雄厚的仗。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Sounds a little bit like another Washington organization with similar acronym, which is the NRA, the National Rifle Association,
sentences.zh: 这听起来有点像华盛顿另一个缩写类似的组织，即NRA，全美步枪协会，

sentences.en: which has kept a very strong lid on efforts to challenge its authority with campaign dollars.
sentences.zh: 它利用竞选资金极大地压制了挑战其权威的努力。

sentences.en: There is a playbook for this sort of behavior, and it is followed pretty clearly.
sentences.zh: 这种行为有一套剧本，而且遵循得非常清晰。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I don't think any of us quite understood it was happening in the housing market.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们谁也没想到这种情况正在房地产市场发生。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And at the end of the day, it wasn't the government.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，这并不是政府的功劳。

sentences.en: that brought them down.
sentences.zh: 这导致了他们的倒台。

sentences.en: And it wasn't a venture capital firm with a ton of money inviting them or trying to be an upstart group.
sentences.zh: 而且这并不是一家拥有巨额资金、试图成为新兴团体的风险投资公司。

sentences.en: It was five normal blue-collar homeowners and a personal injury lawyer from Missouri who had never dealt with the housing market before in his life.
sentences.zh: 这只是五个普通的蓝领房主，加上一位来自密苏里州的个人伤害律师，他这辈子从未接触过房地产市场。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.

sentences.en: So Debra, tell us about this unexpected cast of characters that ends up bringing down the National Association of Realtors.
sentences.zh: 那么黛布拉，给我们讲讲这群意想不到的角色是如何最终让美国房地产经纪人协会倒台的吧。

sentences.en: So Michael,
sentences.zh: 好的，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Well, in 2018, 2019, there was a group of home sellers in Missouri who had learned that they had paid pretty high fees to their real estate agents,
sentences.zh: 嗯，在2018年、2019年，密苏里州有一群卖房者发现他们向房地产经纪人支付了相当高昂的费用，

sentences.en: and they might have a legal case against them.
sentences.zh: 而且他们可能可以起诉对方。

sentences.en: They were probably paying that kind of standard 6% fee to their agents when they sold the house, right?
sentences.zh: 他们在卖房时，大概都支付了那种标准的6%的佣金，对吧？

sentences.en: They were paying the standard 6% fee, but the key was they had not known that that fee was actually negotiable.
sentences.zh: 他们确实支付了标准的6%佣金，但关键在于，他们之前并不知道这笔费用其实是可以协商的。

sentences.en: They thought they had to pay it.
sentences.zh: 他们以为自己必须支付这笔钱。

sentences.en: Okay, here I need to pause.
sentences.zh: 好的，这里我需要暂停一下。

sentences.en: It is actually negotiable?
sentences.zh: 这真的可以协商吗？

sentences.en: It is actually negotiable.
sentences.zh: 确实可以协商。

sentences.en: It is?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes, and that's the thing.
sentences.zh: 没错，问题就在这里。

sentences.en: NAR has always said, we don't set the fees, there is no standard fee.
sentences.zh: 美国房地产经纪人协会（NAR）一直声称，我们不设定费用，没有所谓的标准费用。

sentences.en: But in practice, if consumers don't know that the fee isn't negotiable, and if consumers are told by their agents that they cannot negotiate the fee, that is the fee.
sentences.zh: 但在实践中，如果消费者不知道费用是可以协商的，而且如果经纪人告诉他们费用不能协商，那这就是最终费用。

sentences.en: Okay, so these folks discover that perhaps they didn't need to pay 6% and did, what did they do?
sentences.zh: 好的，所以这些人发现他们可能没必要支付6%的佣金，但还是付了，他们做了什么？

sentences.en: They contacted a lawyer, and they started going through the contracts that they'd signed when they sold their homes.
sentences.zh: 他们联系了一位律师，开始检查他们在卖房时签署的合同。

sentences.en: So one of the people went back through her contract, and the contract actually said, what fee do you want to pay your agent?
sentences.zh: 其中一个人回去翻看了她的合同，合同里竟然写着：你想付给经纪人多少费用？

sentences.en: And it said 6%, 7%, 8%, or 9%.
So she did the smart thing, and she chose the lowest fee, circled 6%, and that's what she paid.
sentences.zh: 于是她做了明智的选择，选了最低的费用，圈出了6%，这就是她支付的金额。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In other words, like a tipping machine that says 20, 22, 25.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就像那种显示20%、22%、25%的小费机一样。

sentences.en: Like when you go buy a coffee and the tip starts at 22%.
sentences.zh: 就像你去买咖啡，小费从22%起步一样。

sentences.en: Right, right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: It's inconceivable whether there's anything beneath that.
sentences.zh: 让人难以置信的是，下面竟然还有其他选项。

sentences.en: Or that you actually could opt out.
sentences.zh: 或者说你其实可以选择不付。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Someone else, he's the son of a factory worker.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个人，他是工厂工人的儿子。

sentences.en: He's now the head of Mothers Against Drunk Driving in Missouri.
sentences.zh: 他现在是密苏里州“母亲反对酒驾”组织的负责人。

sentences.en: These are really blue-collar people.
sentences.zh: 这些人真的是蓝领阶层。

sentences.en: He was told that he was going to be charged 5.5%.
sentences.zh: 他被告知会被收取5.5%的费用。

sentences.en: He found out later that he was charged 6%.
sentences.zh: 后来他发现自己被收了6%。

sentences.en: So his agent just jacked up the fee without telling him.
sentences.zh: 所以他的经纪人在没告诉他的情况下直接提高了费用。

sentences.en: So all these people realized we left money on the table at the most important financial transaction of our entire lives, and we probably have a legal claim against the institution
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些人都意识到，我们在人生中最重要的金融交易中损失了钱，而且我们可能对制定这些规则的机构拥有法律索赔权，

sentences.en: that set the rules that made it so this was possible.
sentences.zh: 正是这些规则导致了这种情况的发生。

sentences.en: And they are.
sentences.zh: 他们确实有。

sentences.en: And they are.
sentences.zh: 他们确实有。

sentences.en: So not only are they upset that they had to pay 6%, and they could have negotiated it and did not know.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们不仅因为不得不支付6%的佣金而感到愤怒，而且他们本可以协商却对此一无所知。

sentences.en: They also are realizing that they have paid the fee to the agent that's representing the person that they're going against in the negotiation for the home sale.
sentences.zh: 他们还意识到，他们支付的佣金是给对方经纪人的，也就是他们在房屋买卖谈判中对立的那一方。

sentences.en: Which is the buyer.
sentences.zh: 也就是买方。

sentences.en: Which is the buyer.
sentences.zh: 也就是买方。

sentences.en: Right, because as you said earlier, the nature of the 6% fee is that it is split between the seller's agent and the buyer's agent, which no one really tells you or reminds you,
sentences.zh: 没错，正如你之前所说，6%佣金的本质是卖方经纪人和买方经纪人平分，这一点没人会真正告诉你或提醒你，

sentences.en: but that's what happens.
sentences.zh: 但事实就是这样。

sentences.en: Because it's all happening through a backdoor on these multiple listing sites that you can only see if you're a real estate agent who belongs to NAR.
sentences.zh: 因为这一切都是通过这些多重上市网站的后门进行的，只有身为NAR成员的房地产经纪人才能看到。

sentences.en: Okay, so what ends up happening to all these sellers once they discover in their minds that they've been wronged and that they want to do something about it?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么当这些卖房者意识到自己受到了不公正对待并想要采取行动时，最终发生了什么？

sentences.en: They hire this attorney, Michael Ketchmark.
sentences.zh: 他们聘请了这位律师，迈克尔·凯奇马克。

sentences.en: He's a personal injury lawyer from Missouri.
sentences.zh: 他是一位来自密苏里州的个人伤害律师。

sentences.en: Pretty much nobody outside of Kansas City had heard of him until this moment.
sentences.zh: 在这一刻之前，堪萨斯城以外几乎没人听说过他。

sentences.en: He decides he's going to file a class action lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 他决定发起集体诉讼。

sentences.en: This is not the best time for NAR.
sentences.zh: 这对NAR来说可不是什么好时机。

sentences.en: This is actually the moment that they were really coming onto my radar as a reporter.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这正是他们作为报道对象进入我视野的时候。

sentences.en: I had spent last summer focused on sexual harassment allegations at NAR, and I discovered that NAR's president, his name was Kenny Parcell,
sentences.zh: 我去年夏天一直在关注NAR内部的性骚扰指控，我发现NAR的主席，名叫肯尼·帕塞尔，

sentences.en: had years and years of sexual harassment accusations against him that had been covered up, and women had been paid off.
sentences.zh: 多年来一直面临性骚扰指控，这些指控被掩盖了，受害女性也得到了封口费。

sentences.en: And at the Times, we published a big expose on those allegations at the end of August, and he stepped down two days later.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》，我们在8月底发表了一篇关于这些指控的大型深度报道，两天后他就辞职了。

sentences.en: Your reporting got the head of this incredibly powerful organization to step down.
sentences.zh: 你的报道让这个极其强大的组织的负责人下台了。

sentences.en: It did, and there have been other resignations since then.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，从那以后还有其他人辞职了。

sentences.en: And that moment for NAR really put them on the world stage.
sentences.zh: 那一刻确实让NAR站在了世界的聚光灯下。

sentences.en: Suddenly people are aware that the leader of the organization is an alleged sexual harasser, and women who've been whistleblowers about the sexual harassment have been paid off.
sentences.zh: 突然间，人们意识到该组织的领导人是一名涉嫌性骚扰的人，而举报性骚扰的女性则被收买了。

sentences.en: And all of that is happening at NAR behind the scenes when this case, where they're being accused of price fixing, ends up going to trial.
sentences.zh: 而当这起被指控操纵价格的案件最终进入审判时，NAR内部正在发生这一切。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Okay, so what ends up happening to this case as it moves through the legal system just as NAR's leader has been forced out.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么当NAR的领导人被迫下台时，这起案件在法律体系中进展如何？

sentences.en: So the case goes forward, and NAR says, okay, we have a new president, we're kind of in disarray, but we are going to regroup, we're going to fight this,
sentences.zh: 案件继续推进，NAR表示，好吧，我们有了新主席，我们现在有点混乱，但我们会重组，我们会抗争，

sentences.en: we're absolutely not going to settle.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对不会和解。

sentences.en: Okay, what ends up happening at this trial?
sentences.zh: 好的，这次审判结果如何？

sentences.en: They come guns blazing, high-powered corporate lawyers, black suits, tons of money, and up against them you have Ketchmark and his team of plaintiffs,
sentences.zh: 他们气势汹汹地来了，带着高薪聘请的企业律师、穿着黑西装、带着巨额资金，而站在他们对立面的是凯奇马克和他的原告团队，

sentences.en: and the jury really liked what Ketchmark had to say.
sentences.zh: 陪审团非常认可凯奇马克的说法。

sentences.en: A Kansas City jury found the National Association of Realtors and other organizations conspired to keep realtor commission fees high.
sentences.zh: 堪萨斯城的陪审团裁定，美国房地产经纪人协会和其他组织串通一气，维持高额的房地产佣金。

sentences.en: They agreed that these home sellers were not told that they could negotiate the prices.
sentences.zh: 他们认同这些卖房者没有被告知他们可以协商价格。

sentences.en: The plaintiffs argued the organizations forced home sellers to pay both the seller and buyer fees, calling that practice wrong and illegal.
sentences.zh: 原告辩称，这些组织强迫卖房者同时支付卖方和买方的佣金，称这种做法是错误且非法的。

sentences.en: So late in October of last year, NAR is found guilty of price fixing.
sentences.zh: 所以去年10月下旬，NAR被判操纵价格罪名成立。

sentences.en: And the jury came back and said, yeah, you're guilty.
sentences.zh: 陪审团回来后说，是的，你们有罪。

sentences.en: and the damages are $1.8 billion.
sentences.zh: 赔偿金额为18亿美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: What we proved was the National Association of Realtors has joined in a conspiracy with the two of the largest corporate real estate brokers to use the system to fix prices.
sentences.zh: 我们证明的是，美国房地产经纪人协会与两家最大的企业房地产经纪公司结成了阴谋，利用该系统操纵价格。

sentences.en: So what happens within hours of this verdict coming through is the floodgates open.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个判决结果出来后的几个小时内，闸门就打开了。

sentences.en: The minute that that verdict came in, we filed a lawsuit against the National Association of Realtors and these other large corporate real estate companies
sentences.zh: 判决下来的那一刻，我们就对美国房地产经纪人协会和其他大型企业房地产公司提起了诉讼，

sentences.en: to bring the same relief nationwide.
sentences.zh: 旨在全国范围内争取同样的赔偿。

sentences.en: Catchmark turns around the same day that he won this case and files a national case.
sentences.zh: 凯奇马克在赢得这起案件的当天就掉转枪头，发起了全国性的诉讼。

sentences.en: So we're talking the exact same argument, but now it's not just Missouri, it's the whole country.
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈论的是完全相同的论点，但现在不仅仅是密苏里州，而是整个国家。

sentences.en: The money will be returned to the homeowners that were the victims of this rigged system.
sentences.zh: 这笔钱将返还给这个被操纵体系的受害者——房主们。

sentences.en: It's been going on in our country for about 100 years, and it stops today.
sentences.zh: 这种情况在我国已经持续了大约100年，今天到此为止。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So every seller in the country.
sentences.zh: 所以全国的卖房者都……

sentences.en: Every single person who's sold a home in the past four years is now part of this case.
sentences.zh: 过去四年里卖过房的每一个人现在都成为了这起案件的一部分。

sentences.en: if they paid a 6% commission and didn't know it.
sentences.zh: 如果他们支付了6%的佣金却对此一无所知的话。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Across the country, already since that case, a case filed by buyers in Illinois, also sellers in Missouri, New York, Texas, and South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 在全国范围内，自那起案件以来，伊利诺伊州的买家，以及密苏里州、纽约州、德克萨斯州和南卡罗来纳州的卖家也提起了诉讼。

sentences.en: There's also an Illinois case that was...
sentences.zh: 还有一个伊利诺伊州的案件是……

sentences.en: Other copycat suits start happening, and within weeks, we're up to almost 20 lawsuits against NAR, all saying, you are a monopoly, you have antitrust violations,
sentences.zh: 其他模仿诉讼开始出现，几周之内，针对NAR的诉讼就达到了近20起，都说你们是垄断者，你们有反垄断违规行为，

sentences.en: and these rules need to change.
sentences.zh: 这些规则必须改变。

sentences.en: It's been a major shakeup in the real estate world today.
sentences.zh: 这对今天的房地产界来说是一次重大的震荡。

sentences.en: If a settlement is approved in court, homes make it cheaper and agents and brokers could be out of business.
sentences.zh: 如果法院批准和解，房屋交易成本会降低，而经纪人和中介可能会失业。

sentences.en: So in the face of all these lawsuits, NAR finally agrees to settle.
sentences.zh: 因此，面对所有这些诉讼，NAR最终同意和解。

sentences.en: And late last week, early Friday morning, they agreed to a settlement that includes massive changes that are going to introduce competition into the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 上周晚些时候，也就是周五清晨，他们达成了一项和解协议，其中包括将为市场引入竞争的重大变革。

sentences.en: The biggest one being the rules that led to that 6% commission are gone.
sentences.zh: 最重要的一点是，导致那6%佣金的规则不复存在了。

sentences.en: Gone?
sentences.zh: 消失了？

sentences.en: Gone.
sentences.zh: 消失了。

sentences.en: So is the 6% fee perhaps now gone?
sentences.zh: 所以6%的费用现在可能消失了吗？

sentences.en: It will.
sentences.zh: 会的。

sentences.en: It will go away because competition is now going to enter the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 它会消失，因为竞争现在将进入市场。

sentences.en: And when competition comes in, people have to lower their fees as a result.
sentences.zh: 当竞争出现时，人们不得不因此降低费用。

sentences.en: A really good example, if you want to look at a precedent in history, is the travel industry.
sentences.zh: 一个很好的例子，如果你想看看历史上的先例，那就是旅游业。

sentences.en: It used to be if you wanted to book a vacation or buy a flight, you had to go through a travel agent.
sentences.zh: 过去，如果你想预订假期或购买机票，你必须通过旅行社。

sentences.en: And you had to pay what they told you to pay.
sentences.zh: 而且你必须支付他们告诉你的价格。

sentences.en: But then we had things enter the marketplace like Expedia and Kayak and Priceline.
sentences.zh: 但后来Expedia、Kayak和Priceline等平台进入了市场。

sentences.en: The same way we now have Zillow and Redfin.
sentences.zh: 就像我们现在有了Zillow和Redfin一样。

sentences.en: We do a lot of the searching for homes ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们自己做了很多搜索房源的工作。

sentences.en: Just not the buying and the selling.
sentences.zh: 只是不包括买卖环节。

sentences.en: But the fees for searching for a home have not changed, even though the service itself has.
sentences.zh: 但搜索房源的费用并没有改变，尽管服务本身已经变了。

sentences.en: It's a lot cheaper now to book travel than it was when you had to go through an agent.
sentences.zh: 现在预订旅行比以前必须通过代理商时便宜多了。

sentences.en: It's going to be a lot cheaper to book a real estate agent now as well to sell your home.
sentences.zh: 现在预订房地产经纪人来卖房也会便宜得多。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I think I understand.
sentences.zh: 我想我明白了。

sentences.en: I want to talk about what it would mean for the 6% commission to go away.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈6%佣金消失意味着什么。

sentences.en: Because as we talked about previously in this conversation, that was the immovable fact of buying and selling a home and a huge amount of money.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们之前谈到的，这是买卖房屋中不可动摇的事实，涉及巨额资金。

sentences.en: A huge amount of money.
sentences.zh: 巨额资金。

sentences.en: Americans spend about $100 billion a year on real estate commissions alone.
sentences.zh: 美国人每年仅在房地产佣金上就花费约1000亿美元。

sentences.en: Unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 难以置信。

sentences.en: Economists forecast that they're probably going to see that number drop by $20 to $50 billion because these commissions are going to go down.
sentences.zh: 经济学家预测，由于佣金将下降，这个数字可能会减少200亿到500亿美元。

sentences.en: But where it really matters is housing prices.
sentences.zh: 但真正重要的是房价。

sentences.en: Housing prices have become higher because real estate commissions are baked into the housing price.
sentences.zh: 房价变得更高，因为房地产佣金被计入了房价中。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。
